evidence: Sidebar lists 19 documents with module badges (UI Components, Core System, API, Data Layer, Authentication) and module filter buttons (All/API/AUTH/DATA/UI/CORE) to browse by module.

Opened "REST API Design Guidelines": shows title, description, "Content Sections" (REST Principles, Endpoint Naming Conventions, Pagination & Filtering) and "Related Documents" list (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide, Rate Limiting).
Expanded "REST Principles" section and clicked "API Versioning Strategy" link; viewer navigated to the API Versioning Strategy document (heading and related docs updated accordingly).
Clicking "REST Principles" header while expanded collapsed it: paragraph content disappeared from the accessibility tree, leaving only the header.
Clicking the collapsed "REST Principles" header again restored the paragraph text and link buttons.

Knowledge Graph tab shows a Modules legend (API, Authentication, Data Layer, UI Components, Core System) and clicking the "HTTP Methods Guide" node selected that document (confirmed by switching to Documents tab, which displayed the HTTP Methods Guide document).
Graph tab renders all 19 document nodes grouped by module in a circular layout with zoom in/out/reset controls and a zoom-percentage indicator (100%, then 140% after zooming).
Top navigation exposes exactly three tabs: Documents, Knowledge Graph, Favorites.

Zoomed graph to 140%, switched to Documents tab and back to Knowledge Graph tab - zoom indicator still read 140%. Section expand/collapse state (sectionStates) and graph zoom are stored in a shared Zustand store confirmed via localStorage key 'tech-docs-storage' (graphState.zoom:1.4, sectionStates populated), consistent across tab switches. Selected document also stayed in sync across tabs (HTTP Methods Guide selected via graph node click was shown when switching to Documents tab).

Favorited "Accessibility Standards" and "REST API Design Guidelines"; nav Favorites badge updated in real time (1 then 2). Applied API module filter + "Last Updated" sort - REST API Design Guidelines still showed "Remove from favorites" (marker retained). localStorage 'tech-docs-storage' contains favorites:["accessibility-standards","rest-api-design"], confirming local persistence. Favorites tab (with filter reset to All) correctly listed both favorited documents.

Knowledge Graph tab shows an SVG graph with nodes (colored by module) connected by edges representing document relationships, with a module color legend, zoom/pan controls, and clickable interactive nodes that navigate to the corresponding document.

Inspected all 19 documents' relatedDocs arrays via source data (src/data/documents.ts fetched through the app's own dev server) - no document's relatedDocs list contains its own id. UI also confirmed: REST API Design Guidelines' Related Documents list never includes itself.

Graph nodes are generated one-to-one from the documents array (19 nodes = 19 documents) grouped/colored by their module field; the Modules legend (API, Authentication, Data Layer, UI Components, Core System) exactly matches the module taxonomy used in the Documents tab filters.

All 19 documents' relatedDocs/section-links reference only valid existing document ids (no broken link exists in current data, so it could not be triggered live). Source inspection of DocumentViewer.handleRelatedDocClick and KnowledgeGraph.handleNodeClick shows both explicitly check getDocumentById(id) and call showToast('...not found','error') without navigating/crashing if the target is missing. Live-tested analogous toast/error-prompt mechanism (clicking a link in a collapsed section shows "Please expand the section to access links" toast without breaking the app), confirming the toast-based graceful-error pattern is functional app-wide.

Section header chevron icon class toggles between "lucide-chevron-down ... transition-transform duration-300" (collapsed) and the same with "rotate-180" appended (expanded), verified via DOM class inspection before/after toggling "REST Principles".

Clicked "HTTP Methods Guide" node in Knowledge Graph tab; switching to Documents tab showed the HTTP Methods Guide document view as the selected/active document, confirming node click navigates to that document's view.
